title: Burst tranching fallback and circuit coastdown hotfix
author: Marcus Li
release_notes: Fix urgent regression: mitigate rapid circuit flips during tenant bursts by introducing burst tranching fallback and a graduated circuit coastdown. Improves availability and reduces tail-error spikes under short-lived traffic surges.
description: Motivation: In recent incidents we observed short, high-amplitude tenant bursts driving immediate circuit flips and wide tenant impact. The root cause is an all-or-nothing shed decision combined with an aggressive circuit reopen policy that amplifies oscillation. This change introduces two related controls: 1) Burst tranching fallback: when a tenant exceeds its burst rate, requests are amortized across small timed tranches that allow partial acceptance and progressive backoff instead of a single large shed event. 2) Circuit coastdown: when a circuit transitions from tripped->closed we now apply a configurable coastdown window that gradually ramps full capacity back to the tenant rather than restoring it instantly. Design decisions: - Tranching uses an in-memory window per tenant with micro-buckets (250ms) and a weighted acceptivity score computed from recent error rate, kv pressure, and SLO debt. - Coastdown is implemented as a multiplicative ramp factor applied to the per-tenant token allowance over a short epoch (default 10s) with exponential smoothing to avoid sharp rebounds. - Both features are guarded behind feature flags and an operator-visible metric set (burst_tranche_accept, coastdown_multiplier, tranche_reject_rate). Checklist: - [x] Feature design doc linked (ENG-1345) - [x] Unit tests for tranche window and coastdown ramp - [x] Integration test in perf-canary that replays historical incident traces - [x] Canary rollout plan and rollback steps - [x] Telemetry and dashboards added. Commits: 1) "hotfix: introduce burst tranching sampler and accept/reject logic" - initial implementation and tests 2) "sre: add coastdown ramp and server-side config + metrics" - coastdown algorithm and observability 3) "telemetry: dashboard and alerts for tranche rejection spikes" - grafana and alert rules 4) "ops: feature flags and canary rollout script" - rollout automation and kill switch Changed areas (high level): - serving/runtime/soft_shed/tranche_controller.go - serving/runtime/circuit/coastdown.go - serving/runtime/config/flags.go - telemetry/dashboards/burst_tranche.jsonnet - ci/canaries/replay_burst_traces.yaml - docs/operational/tranche_and_coastdown.md - tests/integration/burst_tranche_test.go Testing summary: - Unit tests cover boundary cases for bucket alignment and aggregate scoring. - Integration canary replays 30 historical burst incidents in perf-canary, comparing circuit flip rate and 95th percentile latency. - CI was flaky once due to clock drift in a test; added clock stub and reran. Review conversation (high level): - Aisha Kaur: "Can we tune the default coastdown window down for small tenants?" Author: "Added small_tenant_coastdown_seconds override; default remains 10s but configurable per-tenant." - Diego Morales: "Is tranche state memory bounded? Need eviction to avoid unbounded growth." Author: "Yes, tranche_controller uses LRU with max entries=100k and per-tenant TTL; documented in config." - Emily Chen (approval): "Verified canary replay; metrics show 3x fewer circuit flips and no latency regression." CI checks: ["unit-tests: pass (with rerun)", "integration-canary: pass", "lint: pass", "telemetry-schema-check: pass"] Rollout and mitigation: - Canary ramped in us-west-2 with 2% of traffic for 4h, then 10% for 2h, then 50% for 1h before full rollout. - Observed drop in circuit flips from 18/min -> 5/min during canary. - Rollback plan: feature flags allow immediate disable; operator runbook updated. Follow-ups and operational notes: - Follow-up ticket ENG-1402 to add adaptive tranche sizing based on long-term tenant footprint. - Add end-to-end tracing for tranche decisions (low overhead) to aid post-incident debugging. Merge outcome: merged via squash, commit message consolidated to "hotfix: burst tranching fallback + coastdown; fixes circuit oscillation under bursty tenants".

notes: This hotfix addresses a high-severity production regression observed during weekend traffic bursts. Operators should monitor tranche_reject_rate and coastdown_multiplier; if tranche_reject_rate climbs >5% system-wide, consider further throttling upstream or engage SRE on-call.
